summary:
The learning engine is well built. It has one-unknown introductions, follow-ups at about 1.5 and 6 minutes, Leitner boxes, a daily history kept in the save, the dog's warm-up, phrases and listen-and-do. In Villa Sol's story it delivers plenty of practice: the re-run vocab audit measured about 5 active retrievals a minute and 80-90 prompts in a 15-minute session. Four problems undercut real learning:

1. Review supply cannot keep up with demand, and the gap grows. The scheduler's longest interval is 8 days, so 180 words need about 22 reviews a day even for a learner who never forgets. A child exploring the zones gets 6-7 reviews of old words a day. A design rule keeps zone words out of every other place, so the beach's words went almost unused once the run moved to the forest (1, 0 and 2 uses a day).
2. There is almost no spoken recall. Nearly every mic moment shows the word written on a card, or comes right after the word was spoken. "Said aloud" mostly means "read aloud".
3. Stages inflate. The median word turns gold 115 s after it is met, and turns "solid" with any one right tap the next day. 18 of 23 words were solid after 4 days, at a median of 3 uses per word.
4. The parents' "retention" figure comes from 2-4-choice formats whose guessing floor is 33-54%. Some formats cannot be failed at all, so a 70-80% score says little about memory and nothing about recall.

Smaller issues: a forgotten word gets its box back after one right answer 60 s later; zone-first play gets no listen-and-do at all (0 requests in 6 days); the new-word pace has no cap in the open world (20 new words in one 15-minute session); and tools/vocab-audit.js no longer measures the game as it now is. For the 3-year goal, the scheduler and review supply must be fixed before content grows. With the current 8-day maximum, 1000 words means about 114 due reviews a day in year 3. With intervals stretched to 150 days it means about 10.

findings.title: Too few reviews reach a place's words once the child leaves it, and the due backlog grows
findings.evidence: Open-world run (naive bot follows the arrows; warm-up, phrases and listen-and-do on; 6 days of 15 min). Script: scratchpad/audit2/learning/run-open.js; output: analysis-open.txt. The bot left Villa Sol on day 1 (the guide's 'explore') and met 14 beach words on days 1-3. On days 4-6 (forest, park) those 14 words got 1, 0 and 2 uses a day. At the end of day 6, 11 of the 14 had not been used for 3 days. Due words at the end of each day: 13, 11, 5, 12, 18, 25. Old words reviewed each day: 0, 17, 19, 6, 6, 7. Cross-place channels in the code: the warm-up only carries 2-3 words plus a phrase (src/warmup.js:29 and :82). Lola's greeting pool covers only 16 zone words (src/hearts.js:207). Luna's word of the day and Inés's page puzzles happen only in Villa Sol. Every other greeting, favour and listen board uses that person's own place (channels.txt). docs/WORLD_PLAN.md:411 ('never require another zone') keeps zone activities to the zone's own words plus 'universal' ones. Demand from the real scheduler (sim2.txt): 22.5 words due a day at steady state for 180 words, even when every answer is right. With 8 reviews a day the backlog sits at 116-152 words.
findings.impact: A word met in one place is rarely used again while the child plays somewhere else, and spaced retrieval is exactly what turns a met word into a remembered one. The more places and content are added, the bigger this gets. A child who loves exploring will keep meeting words and losing them.
findings.fix: (1) Change the rule from 'never use another zone's words' to 'use any word she has met, wherever it came from': greetings, favours, listen boards and zone props draw first from met words that are due in any place, falling back to the zone's own. (2) Size the warm-up from the backlog (4-8 cards when 15+ words are due), and add a second short review moment mid-session, such as the dog bringing a card at a dog spot. (3) Give Lola, Tomás's letters and the album requests that span every place. (4) Track and show 'due words reviewed a day' against 'due a day'.

findings.title: The longest review interval is 8 days, so the review load grows linearly with vocabulary
findings.evidence: src/words.js:61 W.BOX_DAYS=[0,0,1,2,4,8] and :228 Math.min(5, ...). Real model run in Node (sim3.js / sim3.txt), 1000 words met 1 a day, every review right. As built: 24, 70 and 114 due a day in years 1, 2 and 3. With boxes [0,0,1,3,7,16,35,75,150]: 5.6, 8.2 and 9.7. For 1500 words met 2 a day: 188 vs 11 due a day in year 3. sim1.out.txt C: 180 words steady at 22.5 a day, 1000 words at 125 a day.
findings.impact: At 15 minutes a day the game can supply roughly 25-80 retrievals a session, so the scheduler limits it to a few hundred maintainable words. Without longer intervals, a 3-year build-out (1000-1500 words and phrases) cannot be reviewed. Words either go stale or reviews crowd out everything else.
findings.fix: Extend the boxes to about 1, 3, 7, 16, 35, 75 and 150 days (and make the cap read the array's length instead of 5). Optionally scale each interval by first-try accuracy. Migrate existing saves by mapping box 5 to the new box 5. Do this before adding content.

findings.title: No spoken recall: almost every 'say it' shows the written word, or comes right after hearing it
findings.evidence: Warm-up 'say it (the big mic)' shows the picture, the mic and three word-only cards ('perro / manzana / casa') at the same moment (screenshot evidence_warmup_bigmic_with_written_cards.png; src/warmup.js:189; src/learn.js Choice). The same holds for G.review.ask at stage 2+, Luna's word of the day (display 'text'), the say-it-back bubble (it shows the word and counts as cued), the trick cards in Canelo's menu, the shops, '¿Qué hago?' and '¿Qué toco?'. All are choice cards with labels. Saying the word on a picture-only card comes right after the prompt spoke it, so it is an echo (G.ask echo when masked). Retrievals in the re-run Villa Sol audit (vq.json): said/text 55 (reading a card), said/say 100 (mostly heard-then-said echoes), WordCard 12 echoes. The only picture-to-speech moments with no text: Canelo's care cards (src/pet.js:624) and the phrase slot pictures (evidence_phrase_frame_written_slot_pictures.png). The album (the child's favourite) only plays names and never asks for one (src/album.js). Yet docs/LEARNING_RESEARCH.md §9 says: 'Only spoken recall counts as a level-4 retrieval.'
findings.impact: The child learns to recognise words and to read them aloud, but rarely practises pulling a word out of memory. Producing the word is the hardest and most durable kind of retrieval, and it is what the parent wants: a child who can say words in Spanish. The dashboard's 'said aloud' share hides this.
findings.fix: 'Say first': show the picture and the big mic alone for about 4 s (or until one try), then show the cards as a fallback. Record a spoken answer before the cards appear as its own history letter ('V', voice recall) and require it for gold/solid. Count a word said while its written card is visible as 'read'. Add a '¿Quién es?' recall mode to the album (silhouette, then mic) and to Canelo's care cards. Phrase slots already do this well: reuse that pattern.

findings.title: Stages inflate: gold within about 2 minutes, 'solid' after one right tap the next day
findings.evidence: src/words.js:213-221. Stage 2 comes from any uncued answer, even massed ones. Stage 3 comes from one tap on a word-only card or one page-puzzle match. Stage 4 counts r.ft first tries from before gold, so the two follow-ups on day 1 plus any one first try on day 2 make 3 answers over 2 days. sim1.out.txt A: met, then gold 6 minutes later, then solid after one listen-and-do tap the next day. A2: solid from the page puzzle's forced last pair. Re-run Villa Sol audit (vq.json): met to gold took a median of 115 s (quartiles 73 and 232 s); 48 of 73 words went gold in the session they were met; 32 went solid in the very next session. All 73 met words were solid at the end, as in the committed 2026-10-11 audit. Open run: 18 of 23 met words solid by the end of day 4, at a median of 3 uses per word.
findings.impact: The counts the parent sees (remembered/solid), the card flowers the child sees, and the scheduling (stage-based question forms, the parent check's weak/strong split) all treat words as learned long before memory supports it. The question forms get harder too early and too few, and the parent is misled. The research doc's own rule is '3+ first-try answers on 2+ different days; treat a first right as met, not known'.
findings.fix: Gold needs a recall on a day after the word was met (gap of 1+ day); keep a same-day celebration if wanted, under another name. Solid needs first-try recalls (ideally 'V', above) on 2 later days at least 2 days apart, counting only answers after reaching gold. Listen-and-do taps and forced page matches never count toward gold or solid. Move ft counting after s3.

findings.title: The 'retention' figure counts guessable and unfailable formats, so 70-80% says little
findings.evidence:
src/history.js:136-146 counts the first event of each word on a day it comes back after 1+ days. Every format that can produce that event is a 2-4-choice task:
- 3 cards (warm-up, G.review.ask): 33% guessing floor.
- Luna's word of the day: 4 cards with random-topic distractors.
- Page puzzle: 52% floor, because the last pair is forced and the third is 1 of 2 (src/intro.js:245-252).
- Listen-and-do trays: random taps credit each tested word 50-54% of the time, since a wrong pick still credits the detail it matched (src/listen.js:346; sim4.txt).
- Stage-1 review: plays the word and shows picture+word cards (src/learn.js:338, src/intro.js:189, screenshot evidence_stage1_audio_plus_written_cards.png), so a child who reads can match sound to spelling, and it is still logged as an uncued 'P'.
- Phrase builder taps: always right, logged as a first-try 'P' (src/phrases.js:202).
Open run: 88% retention (45/51) while the median word had 3 uses. On 3 choices, an observed 70% means about 55% real knowledge (p_true = (obs - 1/3)/(2/3)). The parent check is shown only as 'last check', never set beside game retention on the same words.
findings.impact: The parent's main measure of what sticks reads high almost no matter what. It can't detect forgetting or the missing recall, so it can't guide content or pacing decisions over 3 years.
findings.fix: Report two numbers: recognition retention, corrected for guessing (k options), and recall retention (said before any written cue, plus parent checks). Exclude from retention: forced or 1-of-2 page pairs, builder taps, stage-1 sound-to-spelling picks and half-credited listen trays. Show the parent check against the game's numbers for the same words. Set the goal band on the recall number.

findings.title: A forgotten word gets its box back after one right answer a minute later
findings.evidence: src/words.js:241 drops a missed word by only one box and re-asks it in 90 s; :224-228 then moves it up a box on the next uncued first try, counting as ready from 60 s. sim1.out.txt B: a box-5 word missed after 9 days went to box 4, was answered right 60 s later (just after the right answer was shown and spoken) and returned to box 5, next due in 8 days.
findings.impact: A word the child has forgotten is treated as known again on the strength of short-term memory, so the words that most need review get the least. The 'slipping' path only triggers after 3 misses.
findings.fix: On a miss: box = 1 (or max(1, box - 2)), keep the 90-s retry as a same-session relearning step that does not raise the box, and require a right answer on the next day before climbing again. Record lapses per word; the dashboard can show them.

findings.title: Too many new words per session in the open world (the budget was removed)
findings.evidence: src/words.js:298 sets B.OPEN = true, so canIntro is always true. Re-run vocab audit: 'Most new words in any 5 minutes' FAILS at 7 (target ≤5; it passed at 5 on 2026-10-11), and --strict exits 1 (vq-strict.log). Sessions 2 and 6 met 12 and 14 new words. Open run, day 1: 20 new words in one 15-minute session (7 in town, 13 at the beach), against docs/LEARNING_RESEARCH.md R2 (4-6 a session, cap 8).
findings.impact: New words arrive faster than their follow-ups and next-day reviews can be delivered (see the review-supply finding), so most get one same-day use and then fade. It also adds to the stage inflation.
findings.fix: Keep the open world but pace inside it: after about 8 new words in a session, zone introductions (meetW) offer a known word or a review game instead ('¿Qué es esto?' on a met prop), and the guide's next tier favours review activities. Never block exploring. Re-check with the audit.

findings.title: Listen-and-do reaches only 57 of 180 words, needs town words first, and half-credits guesses
findings.evidence: sim4.txt: the request maker's boards can only ever use 57 words. None from greetings, sounds, places, feelings, sea animals, the park's three pages (9 action verbs, playground, bugs), family, body, clothes or mountain animals (channels.txt). Every request needs a known colour, number or size word, which come from Villa Sol chapters or the forest. The open-run child went to the beach on day 1 and got 0 listen-and-do requests in 6 days (G.state.hist.ld.n = 0 every day). At most 2 favours plus 1 warm-up request a day (src/listen.js:503). Under random tapping, each tested word is credited 'understood' 50-54% of the time (sim4.txt).
findings.impact: Understanding whole spoken instructions is the most valuable comprehension practice in the game, and many children will rarely or never get it. Action verbs are the most natural fit for listen-and-do, and none can appear.
findings.fix: Add a board for each place (beach animals and things; park verbs such as 'Salta dos veces', 'Corre rápido'; body and clothes such as 'Toca tu nariz'; mountain animals). Teach 2-3 colours and 1-3 as universal words early, so any first place works. Credit a tested word only on a fully right pick (or only when the pick differs from the answer in that word alone). Let the dog's fetch or play moments be requests.

findings.title: Open-world play has little language when no story beat is going
findings.evidence:
Practice events (the game's own history letters) per minute, including a child's reading and thinking pace:
- Villa Sol story playthrough (re-run audit): about 5.0 a minute (766 active retrievals in 154 game-minutes), 80-90 prompts in a 15-minute session.
- Open run: 1.61 a minute overall (145 events in 90 minutes). By day: 3.8, 1.8, 1.9, 0.6, 0.5, 1.1. The forest days had 9 and 7 events in 15 minutes.
- Event mix: P 43, R 43, S 18, E 7, L 0, m 17.
Caveat: the naive bot only taps visible cues and needed help 16 times (22 times stuck), so this is a lower bound for a child who follows the arrows. Between story beats the guide points at language-free play (fetch, gifts, src/guide.js header).
findings.impact: The child's favourite modes (exploring, the dog, animals) are where practice is thinnest. If most of a 3-year game is free play in a growing world, the minutes spent practising will fall well below what the story-driven numbers suggest.
findings.fix: Make the idle activities carry language: fetch becomes a listen-and-do ('¡Trae la pelota azul!'); dog spots and animals ask a due word ('¿Quién es?', mic first); hide-and-seek finds ask the animal's name. Set a target of 3 or more retrievals a minute in free play, and measure it in the open-world audit (finding below).

findings.title: tools/vocab-audit.js no longer measures the game as it now plays
findings.evidence: It plays Villa Sol's playthrough (tools/playflow.js) and walks back to Villa Sol for free play. It opens the page with the warm-up, phrases and listen-and-do OFF (harness defaults). In the re-run, 107 of 180 words were never met (no zones). It also rewrites docs/VOCAB_AUDIT.md and docs/vocab-timeline.svg on every run; I ran a scratch copy to avoid that: audit2/learning/vocab-audit-copy.js. Quick re-run: 9 of 10 targets pass, the 5-minute target FAILS (7), --strict exits 1. No tool measures practice a minute, due vs reviewed, cross-place review or chance-corrected retention, all of which LEARNING_PLAN_2.md 'How we'll know' relies on.
findings.impact: Without a working measure, content can't be paced and these regressions go unnoticed: the new-word pace, places' words left unreviewed, practice in free play.
findings.fix: Add an open-world audit along the lines of audit2/learning/run-open.js and analyze2.js: several days, a schedule of places, all learning systems on, a child's pace, some wrong taps and speaking. Report events a minute, new words a session, due vs reviewed a day, uses of each place's words while away, chance-corrected retention and the recall share. Write to a scratch path by default and only update docs with a flag.

findings.title: Stage-1 review plays the word and shows it written, so it's a spelling match
findings.evidence: src/learn.js:338 shows stage-1 words as picture+word cards while the prompt plays the word ('¿🔊?'). src/intro.js:189 and src/warmup.js:188 use this for every stage-1 review, including Canelo's first follow-up of every new word. Screenshot evidence_stage1_audio_plus_written_cards.png: she hears 'concha' and sees 'concha / pan / gato' with pictures. Learn.js cue() only checks the prompt's own text and picture, so this is logged uncued ('P'), moves the word to stage 2 'known', and counts for retention.
findings.impact: A child who reads well can answer without linking the sound to its meaning. The first spaced retrieval of every word is weaker than the model believes, and 'known' is reached by decoding.
findings.fix: Use the slipping-word format (G.intro.again) for stage 1: hear it and pick among picture-only cards, with the word shown on the right card only after the pick. Or log this format as cued 'K' so it doesn't count.

findings.title: The page puzzle's last pair is credited as a first-try recall
findings.evidence: src/intro.js:245-252 credits every pair as answerRight(mode 'match', first try). Once three pairs are matched, the last is forced; the third is 1 of 2. A child who knows nothing gets 52% first-try matches ((1/4+1/3+1/2+1)/4). 'match' counts as recall, so it can make a word gold (sim1 A3: met, picked, matched 30 s later = gold) or solid (sim1 A2), and it counts for retention. Page puzzles were 152 of 818 prompts in the re-run audit.
findings.impact: About a fifth of all prompts give inflated credit, which feeds the stage and retention inflation above.
findings.fix: Don't credit the last pair (it still grows the card for fun), or add a fifth decoy picture so no pair is forced. Count a match as recognition, not recall.

findings.title: The review engine picks the lowest box first, so long-interval words wait longest when time is short
findings.evidence: src/words.js:276-282 G.review.due sorts group 2 by box (ascending) before lateness. With 8 reviews a day for 180 words (sim2.txt), by day 45 the oldest unreviewed word was 41 days since its last use with the engine's order vs 19 days when sorted by lateness. Greetings and favours use G.review.next.
findings.impact: When review supply is short (the normal case, above), words at the longest intervals, the ones closest to long-term memory, are the ones left to lapse.
findings.fix: Sort by the ratio of days since last use to the box's interval (most overdue relative to its interval first), with just-met follow-ups and missed words still first.

findings.title: Phrase stats count tapping and reading: the frame is always written, and the builder can't fail
findings.evidence: PhraseAsk always writes the frame in her speech bubble and on the frame card ('Quiero ?', screenshot evidence_phrase_frame_written_slot_pictures.png), so saying the whole phrase is reading the frame plus recalling the slot word. The builder (tap the frame, then a word) is logged as a first-try 'P' for the phrase (src/phrases.js:202): it moves stage 1 to 2 and counts as retained when it is the day's first event. Open run: in 6 days 4 of 6 patterns were introduced (¿Dónde está? and Tengo never came up), with about 14 phrase events in total.
findings.impact: Phrase progress on the dashboard overstates spoken ability. The six patterns get little practice in total (a couple of events a day).
findings.fix: Log builder taps as cued ('K'). Once a phrase is gold, fade the frame text (show only the speech bubble and the slot picture) so saying it becomes recall. Put phrases in the routines that recur daily (every greeting, every shop, the dog's fetch), not one-off moments.

findings.title: The 'said aloud' share is inflated by repeated dog commands and echoes
findings.evidence: src/history.js:141 counts S, s and E (echo) as said. src/pet.js:415 and :616 log a new 'S' every time a trick is said at Canelo's menu (the star is once a day, the history event is every time, up to H.EVMAX = 60 per word per day). Echoes ('E': the gold card's mic, saying a word just heard) also count toward 'said aloud', which the plan targets at more than a third of practice.
findings.impact: Commanding the dog 20 times can make the share look healthy without any other word being said, so the target is easy to hit for the wrong reason.
findings.fix: For the share, count each word's spoken events once a day and leave out echoes. Better, report the 'V' recall share proposed above as the speaking metric.

**Practice budget for the 3-year question**
- Story-paced play gives about 75-90 retrievals in 15 minutes. Free play gave about 24.
- At 75 a day over 3 years, that is about 82,000 retrievals.
- With intervals stretched to 150 days, maintenance for 1000-1500 words is about 10-16 a day. That leaves most of a session for new learning: roughly 1-2 new items a day, about 1,000-1,500 items over 3 years.
- With the current 8-day maximum, maintenance alone needs 114-188 a day by year 3, which no 15-minute session can supply.
